analysis:
The only change in ProviderLoop.swift adds two internal actor-isolated stored properties at head lines 451-454: `releasedAdmissions: [String: ReleasedAdmission]` and `coldLoadReleasesWorkFIFO = WorkFIFOPolicy.releasesColdLoadWaits()`. The surrounding base and head units (the other stored state, init and companion-file list) are unchanged. The visible diff contains no new cryptography, key handling, attestation, App Attest authorization (T-053/T-054), plaintext exposure (T-008) or prefix-cache storage change (T-041). Cache TTL, HMAC naming and the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE gate are not touched.

The new state supports work-FIFO release during cold model loads, implemented in ProviderLoop+WorkFIFO.swift and WorkFIFOPolicy, which are not supplied. That policy could affect availability (T-010, T-029) and request ordering and admission. It could also affect ordering around disconnect, cancellation and update drains. A request that releases its FIFO slot during a model-load wait but is not tracked in `releasedAdmissions` through reconnect, cancellation or draining could bypass admission gates, so the next pass should check how that map is cleaned up on error and cancellation. `releasesColdLoadWaits()` may read an environment variable, and its default is not visible here. Without the companion code I cannot conclude there is a regression, so I am recording an unverified contract rather than a finding. No finding qualifies on the supplied evidence, and I recommend deeper review of the companion files for admission, cancellation, leak and starvation behavior.
